The shot starts from a high-altitude aerial wide view using a first-person drone perspective, slowly pushing forward over an ancient Chinese palace complex covered in light mist. The architecture is dominated by green tiled roofs and red walls, with lakes and courtyards softened by atmospheric fog. The camera follows a single continuous motion with no cuts or abrupt changes, maintaining a steady forward push as the core movement.

The camera gradually descends while moving forward, entering layers of drifting fog. Mist naturally passes across the frame edges, creating soft occlusion and immersive depth without aggressive transitions. It then moves into a mid-level height glide above the lake, where reflections and shoreline trees slowly slide past both sides of the frame, reinforcing spatial movement without low-altitude extreme speed or complex orbiting.

The motion continues toward the central axis of the palace, where the main hall gradually grows in scale and dominance, naturally tightening the composition from open space to focused depth. The entire movement must remain stable, linear, and continuous, avoiding orbit, rapid altitude shifts, or multi-directional camera behavior, emphasizing a calm, immersive traversal through an oriental misty architectural world.
